info.title: Song provider API
info.summary: What a server answers so that Oneverse can look songs up in it.
info.description:
A server to this description can be added in Oneverse's Admin > Plugins > Song provider: Oneverse then asks it for song info (Auto detect), artwork, artists' pictures, and chords with lyrics (Find chords), for the hooks the admin chose among those it answers.

- Oneverse calls it from its server: over HTTPS on a public address, unless the admin said it's on the same network. It never follows a redirect, reads at most 2 MB of an answer, and waits 8 seconds at most.
- Answers are JSON. Fields Oneverse doesn't know are ignored, so a server can add its own; one that doesn't fit is refused as a whole, never guessed at.
- Images (artwork, pictures) are downloaded by Oneverse's server only from this server's own address (same origin as the address the admin entered) or a music service's image host.
- An example server, dependency-free, is in Oneverse's repository: examples/song-provider/server.mjs.

servers.description: The address an admin enters, without /v1 (with it works too).

get.summary: Who it is and what it answers
get.description: Asked when the server is added and on Test connection. A hook it doesn't list is never asked.

401.description: No key, or not one it takes.

429.description: Too many requests: Oneverse tries again later.

default.description: Anything else: said to the admin as this provider's error.

post.description: For Auto detect, the artwork search and Find chords. Best matches first. For Find chords, only songs with chords are shown: `hasContent: true`, or `versions` listed. Versions are shown under their song, the best rated first, with where each comes from.

default.description: Anything else: said to the admin as this provider's error.

get.description: When a match is chosen in Auto detect, and with its chords and lyrics.

get.description: As ChordPro text, or as a SongDocument v2 (https://github.com/Vulcio/Oneverse/blob/main/docs/song-document-v2.md), which Oneverse checks as it checks a stored song. `rights` is shown to the person taking the chart.

parameters.description: The provider's own ID for the song, as its search gave it.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: One of the song's `versions`, by its ID; left out, the song's default chart.

bearer.description: The key the admin entered, if any: `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Kept encrypted by Oneverse.

apiVersion.description: The version of this API it speaks: 1.

name.description: Its name, shown in Oneverse unless the admin gives it another.

provides.description: What it answers: songInfo (search and songs/{id}), artwork (artworkUrl in its songs), artistPictures (artists/picture), chords (songs/{id}/content).

languages.description: The languages its songs are in, as BCP 47 tags ("en", "fr").

language.description: The language wanted, as a BCP 47 tag, when the person said.

limit.description: At most this many songs; it may send fewer.

id.description: Its own ID for the song, used in /v1/songs/{id}.

key.description: Its key as a chord name: G, Bb, F#m.

thumbnailUrl.description: A small picture to show among results.

artworkUrl.description: Its artwork, full size, on this server's own address or a music service's image host.

url.description: The song's page on its site, for people.

hasContent.description: Whether /v1/songs/{id}/content has its chords and lyrics.

versions.description: Its charts, when it has several, each with its rating and where it comes from. Listed: the song has chords even without hasContent. None listed: one chart, if hasContent.

id.description: Its own ID for this version, sent as ?version= to /v1/songs/{id}/content.

name.description: What sets it apart, as people call it: Original, Acoustic, Simplified.

key.description: Its key as a chord name: G, Bb, F#m.

capo.description: The fret the capo goes on, when the chart is played with one.

count.description: How many people rated it; shown, and weighs the rating when versions are ordered.

source.description: Where this version comes from, when the server gathers charts from other sites or people: shown as "from <name>".
